title: Electric & Horse Fencing
excerpt: Plan your power supply, fence layout and visibility before choosing electric fencing for horses or livestock.

sections.title: How electric fencing works
sections.text: An energiser sends pulses along the fence wire. Contact with the wire completes a circuit through the animal and the ground. Electric fencing acts as a psychological barrier, making the fence layout and its visibility important considerations for horses.

sections.title: What to plan
items: Power supply: mains, battery or solar.
The total length of fence wire.
The style of fence and the animals you want to keep in or out.
A map of the area, including gates and fence lines.

sections.title: Visibility and equipment
sections.text: Horse sighter wire, tapes, braids and suitable energisers are among the options to discuss with our team. Bring your layout and requirements so we can help you choose products for the job.

title: Automatic Gates
excerpt: Explore sliding and swing gates, mains or solar power, and the accessories available for your entrance.

sections.title: Sliding and swing gates
sections.text: Our workshop manufactures sliding and swing gates. Automation equipment is available for mains-powered and solar-powered installations.

sections.title: Power and accessories
sections.text: Solar collectors need a position in full sun for optimum operation. Gate automation accessories include remote controls, wireless keypads, photocells, flashing lamps and antennas.

sections.title: Discuss your entrance
sections.text: Talk to our team about your gate and power supply. Our Gatemaster Australia website provides more information about gate motors, gates, hardware and accessories.

title: Gates & Frames
excerpt: Bring the right measurements and hardware details when choosing a farm gate, horse gate or custom frame.

sections.title: Before you order
sections.text: A gate needs to suit both its purpose and the posts supporting it. Our team can help you compare gate styles and fittings.

sections.title: Your gate checklist
items: The purpose and style of the gate.
The height and width of the opening.
Frame size or nominal bore.
Mesh type and finish: galvanised, PVC coated or powder coated.
Hinge type and fastening.
Post material and shape: timber or steel, square or round.

sections.title: Custom gate work
sections.text: Alongside farm and horse gates, our workshop makes special-order and decorative gates. Bring your opening measurements and preferred style when discussing a custom gate.

title: Fencing & Security Wire
excerpt: Match your wire or mesh to the fence purpose, post layout and gate requirements.

sections.title: Start with the purpose
sections.text: Wire and mesh should suit what the fence needs to do. Options include field fencing, chain link, welded mesh and woven netting, with different openings and wire sizes.

sections.title: Details to bring
items: Required fence height and intended lifespan.
Post type and spacing.
Corner and end straining arrangements.
Gate requirements.
Footing requirements for end and corner posts.

sections.title: Mesh, netting and smaller jobs
sections.text: Welded mesh is available in panels, while stock fencing and netting are supplied in rolls. Smaller rolls of mesh and netting can suit garden and enclosure projects. Discuss the animals, opening size and fence layout with our team before selecting a product.

title: Fencing Pickets & Posts
excerpt: Compare steel, treated pine and post-and-rail options, and consider the ground conditions and fence weight.

sections.title: Posts provide the structure
sections.text: Fence posts contribute to the strength and appearance of a fence. Wire choice influences post spacing; soil conditions and fence weight influence how the posts are installed.

sections.title: Choosing a style
sections.text: Steel pickets and galvanised pipe posts suit many rural fencing applications. Treated pine post-and-rail and PVC post-and-rail offer other styles to consider for a property.

sections.title: Fittings and tools
sections.text: Post rammers, post lifters and fence droppers are among the tools and accessories used in fencing. Galvanised pipe posts also require suitable fittings and connectors. Include corner posts, end posts and gates in your plans when discussing the materials you need.

title: Fencing Tools & Wire Accessories
excerpt: An overview of tools for handling, joining, tensioning and fastening fencing wire.

sections.title: Tools for the job
sections.text: Wire spinners, chain strainers and wire tensioning systems are used in rural fencing work. Smaller jobs may call for netting clips, wire twisting tools or handyman wire strainers.

sections.title: Tools and accessories to discuss
items: Wire spinners and chain strainers.
Wire and netting strainers.
Wire joiners and tensioners.
Netting clips and barbed staples.
Fencing pliers, twisting tools and bolt cutters.

sections.title: Ask for guidance
sections.text: Tell our team which wire and fence system you are using so we can help identify suitable tools and accessories. Ask about the Rural Fencing Guide when planning your project.

title: Aviaries & Pet Enclosures
excerpt: Explore mesh, modular frames and enclosure panels for aviaries, chicken runs and small-pet projects.

sections.title: Mesh and framework
sections.text: Meshes and netting come in different weights, sizes and openings for projects such as aviaries, rabbit hutches and chicken runs. Modular connectors for square tubing offer a framework option that can be dismantled and stored.

sections.title: Panel enclosures
sections.text: Welded-mesh enclosure panels can be joined with fence clamps to create different layouts. Gate panels provide access, and some panels have closer-spaced lower wires for smaller pets. Check panel dimensions and mesh openings against the animals you need to contain.

sections.title: Bring your layout
sections.text: Bring the enclosure dimensions and details of the animals when asking for advice. Posts, gates, fittings and feeding bowls are other items to consider alongside the mesh and framework.

title: Pumps & Irrigation
excerpt: A practical checklist of water-source, pipework and power details to bring when choosing irrigation equipment.

sections.title: Plan the system
sections.text: We supply irrigation products for domestic and agricultural applications. A few details about your site will help our team advise on pumps, pipework and irrigation equipment.

sections.title: Information to bring
items: Water source: mains, tank, dam, bore, creek or river.
The pump type you are considering and whether a submersible pump is needed.
Water levels and the head the pump needs to handle.
Length and diameter of the irrigation lines.
The sprinkler type.
Available power, including mains or solar.
Whether timers are required.

sections.title: Discuss the whole setup
sections.text: Bring these details when visiting or contacting us, so the equipment can be considered as part of your irrigation system.

title: Shade Cloth, Weed Mat & Bird Netting
excerpt: Explore fabric products for shade, garden coverage and bird exclusion, together with their fixing accessories.

sections.title: Fabric options
sections.text: The range described on our information pages includes shade cloth, shade sails, bin covers, weed mat and bird netting. These products serve different purposes, so start with the area you need to cover and what you want the fabric to do.

sections.title: Fixings and supports
sections.text: Associated hardware includes wire rope, turnbuckles, shackles and hooks. Posts and cement may also form part of a project.

sections.title: Discuss your project
sections.text: Ask our team about the available fabric weights, colours and sizes, along with the fixing accessories for your intended application.

title: Garden & Household Projects
excerpt: Ideas for using mesh, netting, weed mat and modular framing around the house and garden.

sections.title: Beyond the farm fence
sections.text: Many fencing and hardware products can also be useful in the garden. Small rolls of mesh and wire netting can help form enclosures, while tie wire and weed mat have a range of garden uses.

sections.title: Modular project ideas
sections.text: Connectors for square tubing can be used to assemble structures that are easy to dismantle and store. Examples include aviaries, small-pet cages, shade houses, shelves, screens and compost bins.

sections.title: Tools and materials
sections.text: Garden tools, fly screen, clothes line and shade products are other options to discuss. Bring the dimensions and intended use of your project so our team can help you work through the materials.

title: Materials for Rural Projects
excerpt: A starting point for discussing posts, tubing, mesh and fittings for rural and backyard projects.

sections.title: Frames and mesh
sections.text: The existing information page illustrates rural projects using steel posts, galvanised tubing and mesh panels. It includes examples such as hutches, chicken runs and a stable door made with tubing and timber.

sections.title: Materials to discuss
items: Galvanised pipe posts and struts.
Square tubing and suitable connectors.
Welded-mesh panels and tie wire.
Cement and project-specific fittings.

sections.title: Bring your project details
sections.text: Use these examples as a starting point for a discussion about materials. Tell our team what you are building and bring your measurements or plans.

title: Choosing Castors & Wheels
excerpt: Check the load, surface, wheel size and fixing method before choosing wheels or castors.

sections.title: Match the wheel to its use
sections.text: Wheels and castors come in different sizes and materials, including rubber, nylon, polyurethane and steel. The right choice depends on the job and the surface on which it will move.

sections.title: Selection checklist
items: Required load-bearing capacity.
Wheel size.
The surface where it will be used.
Fixed, swivel or braked operation.
Attachment method: an axle for a wheel, or a mounting plate for a castor.

sections.title: Bring the details
sections.text: Have these details ready when asking our team about the available options.
